_comment: Tier -> concrete target, per provider. A tier is plain text, or {text, agent, model, efforts}: core.resolve_tier() clamps the decided effort into 'efforts' (so it is always valid for that model) and fills {agent}/{model}/{effort} into 'text'. When 'agent' + 'efforts' are set, the agent actually invoked is '<agent>-<effort>' - these variants are GENERATED by `python router/skills_hub.py agents` (Claude: ~/.claude/agents/*.md with model+effort frontmatter; Codex: ~/.codex/agents/*.toml + [agents.*] in config.toml). Hooks cannot switch the running model/effort in any of the three tools, so delegating to such a fixed-model, fixed-effort agent is how the decision is actually enforced. Model names verified 2026-09-23: Claude generic aliases (models.json policy), Codex ~/.codex/models_cache.json, Antigravity `agy models`.

tiers.main: Answer directly in this session; do not spawn a subagent.

fast.text: Delegate the work to the `{agent}` subagent ({model}, effort {effort}).

sonnet.text: Delegate the work to the `{agent}` subagent ({model}, effort {effort}).

test.text: Delegate the work to the `{agent}` subagent ({model}, effort {effort}).

deep.text: Delegate the work to the `{agent}` subagent ({model}, effort {effort}).

cli:codex.text: Use the `cli-bridge` skill to run this task with Codex (`--model {model} --effort {effort}`).

cli:antigravity.text: Use the `cli-bridge` skill to run this task with Antigravity (`--model {model}`).

verify.codex: Then get an independent review of the result via the `cli-bridge` skill (codex, `--model gpt-5.6-terra --effort high`).
verify.antigravity: Then have Antigravity solve it independently via the `cli-bridge` skill (antigravity, `--model gemini-3.1-pro-high`) and compare; report any disagreement.

tiers.main: Answer directly in this session with the current model.

fast.text: Trivial request: answer directly and briefly, no subagent, minimal reasoning.

deep.text: Spawn a subagent with agent_type `{agent}` ({model}, reasoning effort {effort}) to do this work, then report its result.

antigravity._comment: Antigravity has no custom-agent mechanism with a fixed model (verified: `agy agents` lists none, docs cover only skills/hooks/rules/plugins/MCP), so its tiers are advisory text; the effort is baked into the model name (e.g. gemini-3.8-flash-low). The cli-bridge (agy -p --model X) is where Claude actually enforces an Antigravity model.

fast.text: Trivial request: answer directly and briefly. Best-fit model: `{model}`.

deep.text: Hard request: plan first, then work step by step and verify. Best-fit model: `{model}` (or claude-opus-4-6-thinking); if the current model is a Flash model, tell the user to switch with /model.

claude-chat._comment: Claude desktop Chat/Cowork via the MCP route_prompt tool: no hooks, no subagents, and the model cannot switch itself - so tiers are advice (reasoning discipline + which model the user may pick in the model menu).

tiers.fast: Simple request: answer directly and concisely.
tiers.sonnet: Answer directly (Sonnet is a good fit).
tiers.test: Testing task: back every claim with actual run output where tools allow.

deep.text: Hard request: plan first, reason step by step and verify before answering. If the current model is not {model}, suggest the user switch to {model} with extended thinking.

tiers.cli:codex: If a Codex/ChatGPT second opinion would help, say so; otherwise answer directly.
tiers.cli:antigravity: Long-context request: work through the material section by section.

verify.codex: Double-check the result critically before presenting it.
verify.antigravity: Double-check the result critically before presenting it.
